transfer.interpretation: Full-source nearest point within the existing 6 m display simplification allowance; all interpolation contributors within 5 m of that same point; full-source camera visibility to 0.05 m. These are acceptance bounds, not source accuracy estimates.

metadata.label: AMICA mosaic
metadata.coverage: Ten Hayabusa AMICA v-band photographs from September and October 2005. The established brightness-reference frame comes first, then close-ups take priority over distant views. Registered through the archived Gaskell Cartesian backplanes. Brightness is approximately normalized and matched across overlaps; photographed shadows and seams remain. The grid marks unsupported surface coverage.

celestial.sunSource: Pinned JPL Horizons heliocentric elements and the source mission body-fixed rotation model

controls.label: AMICA mosaic
controls.notes: Eight Hayabusa AMICA v-band photographs from September and October 2005, including closer views from north and south of the equator. Registered through the archived Gaskell Cartesian backplanes. Brightness is approximately normalized and matched across overlaps; photographed shadows remain. The grid marks unsupported surface coverage.

controls.label: Elevation
controls.notes: Color shows radius minus a 165 m reference sphere, including the body's broad irregular shape. This is not gravitational height or an image observation. Brightness adds cartographic relief from the full source model; Shadows adds approximate fixed-epoch Sun lighting. Fine terrain is represented in the map while the displayed silhouette is simplified. Values follow the nearest corresponding point on the full source shape within the display mesh’s simplification allowance. This is radial height, not gravitational height; flat previews withhold overlapping radial surfaces.
